jp: 田中[たなか]さん{は|wa-topic}毎朝[まいあさ]コーヒー{を|o-object}飲[の]みます{か|ka-question}。
en: Does Mr. Tanaka drink coffee every morning?
why: か at the end of a sentence turns it into a question; よ and ね would make it a statement.

jp: これ{は|wa-topic}あなた{の|no-possessive}かさです{か|ka-question}。
why: か makes the polite sentence a yes/no question; よ would assert it and ね would ask for agreement.

jp: 駅[えき]{は|wa-topic}どこです{か|ka-question}。
why: A question word needs か at the end of a polite question.

jp: 今[いま]何時[なんじ]です{か|ka-question}。
why: か closes a question; a sentence-ending よ or ね would not ask for the time.

jp: 昨日[きのう]{は|wa-topic}何[なに]{を|o-object}しました{か|ka-question}。
why: The question word 何 plus か asks what happened; the other endings make a statement.

jp: 明日[あした]{の|no-possessive}パーティー{に|ni-destination}来[き]ます{か|ka-question}。
en: Are you coming to tomorrow's party?
why: か turns 来ます into a question; ね would only seek confirmation of something already assumed.

jp: 名前[なまえ]{は|wa-topic}何[なん]です{か|ka-question}。
why: か is the question marker that completes 何ですか; the other endings give a statement.

jp: 学校[がっこう]{まで|made-until}バス{で|de-means}行[い]きます{か|ka-question}。
en: Do you go to school by bus?
why: か makes the sentence a yes/no question about how the listener travels.

jp: 日本語[にほんご]{は|wa-topic}難[むずか]しいです{か|ka-question}。
why: か after です asks whether the statement is true; よ would insist that it is difficult.

jp: 誰[だれ]{が|ga-question}この絵[え]{を|o-object}描[か]きました{か|ka-question}。
why: か ends the question that starts with the question word 誰; the other endings state or confirm.

jp: ご飯[はん]{は|wa-topic}もう食[た]べました{か|ka-question}。
why: か turns 食べました into a question about whether it has already happened.

jp: 週末[しゅうまつ]{は|wa-topic}何[なに]{を|o-object}する予定[よてい]です{か|ka-question}。
en: What are you planning to do this weekend?
why: The question word 何 and a final か form a question; the other endings state a plan.

jp: この電車[でんしゃ]{は|wa-topic}新宿[しんじゅく]{に/へ|ni-destination}行[い]きます{か|ka-question}。
en: Does this train go to Shinjuku?
why: か makes it a question; よ would tell the listener that it goes there.

jp: あの人[ひと]{は|wa-topic}誰[だれ]です{か|ka-question}。
why: か completes the question started by 誰; the other endings state or confirm.

jp: 毎日[まいにち]何時間[なんじかん]日本語[にほんご]{を|o-object}勉強[べんきょう]します{か|ka-question}。
en: How many hours a day do you study Japanese?
why: か ends the question about how many hours; the other endings turn it into a statement.

jp: 手紙[てがみ]{は|wa-topic}もう出[だ]しました{か|ka-question}。
en: Have you already sent the letter?
why: か asks whether the letter has been sent; よ would say it has.

jp: 先生[せんせい]{は|wa-topic}どんな音楽[おんがく]{が|ga-stative}好[す]きです{か|ka-question}。
en: What kind of music does the teacher like?
why: か follows 好きです to ask what kind of music; the other endings would state the answer.

jp: 山田[やまだ]さん{は|wa-topic}学生[がくせい]です{か|ka-question}。
why: か makes it a plain yes/no question; ね would say you assume she is a student.

jp: 牛乳[ぎゅうにゅう]{は|wa-topic}冷蔵庫[れいぞうこ]{に|ni-location}ありました{か|ka-question}。
en: Was there any milk in the fridge?
why: か asks whether the milk was there; the other endings assert or assume it.

jp: 今日[きょう]{は|wa-topic}寒[さむ]いです{か|ka-question}。
why: か asks whether it is cold; よ or ね would state that it is.

jp: すみません、トイレ{は|wa-topic}どこ{に|ni-location}あります{か|ka-question}。
en: Excuse me, where is the restroom?
why: The question word どこ with a final か forms the question; the other endings do not ask anything.

jp: 切符[きっぷ]{は|wa-topic}いくらです{か|ka-question}。
why: か marks the question that いくら sets up.

jp: 明日[あした]{は|wa-topic}一緒[いっしょ]に昼[ひる]ご飯[はん]{を|o-object}食[た]べません{か|ka-question}。
en: Won't you have lunch with me tomorrow?
why: ませんか is a polite invitation; か keeps it a question, while よ or ね would assert it.

jp: 試験[しけん]{は|wa-topic}いつです{か|ka-question}。
why: か marks the question that いつ sets up.

jp: お母[かあ]さん{は|wa-topic}お元気[げんき]です{か|ka-question}。
why: か makes the polite sentence a question about her health.

jp: 窓[まど]{を|o-object}開[あ]け{ても|te-mo}いいです{か|ka-question}。
why: The permission pattern ても いいです asks a question when it ends in か.

jp: 昨日[きのう]{の|no-possessive}テスト{は|wa-topic}どうでした{か|ka-question}。
why: か ends a question with どう.

jp: 夏休[なつやす]み{に|ni-time}どこ{に/へ|ni-destination}行[い]きました{か|ka-question}。
en: Where did you go in the summer vacation?
why: か makes どこへ行きました a question; the other endings state a fact.

jp: お兄[にい]さん{は|wa-topic}何歳[なんさい]です{か|ka-question}。
en: How old is your older brother?
why: か completes the question word 何歳; the other endings do not ask.

jp: 図書館[としょかん]{で|de-place}何[なに]{を|o-object}借[か]りました{か|ka-question}。
en: What did you borrow at the library?
why: か closes the 何 question; the others would turn it into a statement.

jp: このカレー{は|wa-topic}辛[から]いです{か|ka-question}。
why: か asks whether it is spicy; よ or ね would assert it.

jp: 昨日[きのう]{は|wa-topic}誰[だれ]{と|to-with}映画[えいが]{を|o-object}見[み]ました{か|ka-question}。
en: Who did you see a movie with yesterday?
why: か closes the question started by 誰; the other endings would make a statement.

jp: 荷物[にもつ]{は|wa-topic}重[おも]いです{か|ka-question}。
why: か makes a yes/no question about the luggage.
